9758               	;
9759               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9760               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9761               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9762               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9763               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9764               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9765               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9766               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9767               	; 	'
9768               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9769               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9770               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9771               	; 	'
9772               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9773               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9774               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9775               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9776               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9777               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9778               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9779               	; 	'
9780               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9781               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9782               	; 	'
9783               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9784               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9785               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9786               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9787               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9788               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9789               	; 	'
9790               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9791               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9792               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9793               	; 	' before any of this.
9794               	; 	'
9795               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9796               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9797               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
9798               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
9799               	; 	' journey.
9800               	; 	'
9801               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
9802               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
9803               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.
9804               	; 	pacc = hacc

     DBF2 21B7     
     DBF4 212C

10240 DF5E 0450  20 	b *r0
10241               	;
10242               	; 	' ======================================================================
10243               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10244               	; 	' ======================================================================
10245               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10246               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10247               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10248               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10249               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10250               	; 	'
10251               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10252               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10253               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10254               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10255               	; 	' broken.
10256               	; 	'
10257               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10258               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10259               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10260               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10261               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10262               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10263               	; 	'
10264               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10265               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10266               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10267               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10268               	; coll_obst:
10269               cvb_COLL_OBST
10270               	; 	IF klst = ST_ESC THEN RETURN		' riding is invincible, per the

10762               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
10763               	; 	'
10764               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
10765               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10766               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10767               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10768               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10769               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10770               	; 	'
10771               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10772               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10773               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
10774               	; 	'
10775               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
10776               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
10777               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
10778               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10779               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
10780               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
10781               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

10887               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.
10888               	; 	'
10889               	; 	' This test used to sit AFTER his sprites had been written, so every pass
10890               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
10891               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
10892               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
10893               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
10894               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
10895               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
10896               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
10897               	; 	'
10898               	; 	' Deciding BEFORE drawing costs one test and cannot race the ISR at all:
10899               	; 	' the mirror never holds a position to be caught with.
10900               	; 	IF klst = ST_ELEV THEN

11502               	; 	' half, so both boxes span rows 0-15 and neither can be tucked away --

11507               	; 	' HE RISES A PIXEL ON THE RECOVERY BEATS. A runner is highest at mid-flight
11508               	; 	' and lowest at contact; with the body pinned at a constant y, alternating
11509               	; 	' legs under a motionless torso reads as a dance rather than as travel.
11510               	; 	'
11511               	; 	' One pixel is enough at this size, and it lifts the BODY ONLY -- the legs
11512               	; 	' keep their y, so the planted foot stays on the floor and the figure
11513               	; 	' stretches at the waist instead of hopping. Lifting the legs too would be
11514               	; 	' a jump.
11515               	; 	'
11516               	; 	' Beats 2 and 4 are the recoveries, which is exactly `hanim AND 8` -- the
11517               	; 	' cycle's LOW beat bit. IT MUST MOVE WITH THE BEAT BITS ABOVE IT: on the
11518               	; 	' wrong bit he rises and falls twice per stride, a second clock inside one
11519               	; 	' figure, which is the flapping of DESIGN.md 0j2 in the vertical.
11520               	; 	'
11521               	; 	' Safe because HARRY'S COLLISION HAS NO VERTICAL COMPONENT: he is caught on
11522               	; 	' `same level AND |dx| < CATCHR`. Doing this to Kelly would desynchronise
11523               	; 	' his sprite from the ball and biplane windows in DESIGN.md 5a, which is
11524               	; 	' why it is not done to him.

11526               	; 	' away from the feet. Two reasons, and the second was not the first plan:
11527               	; 	'

11530               	; 	'   * Lifting the body alone opens a one-pixel gap at the waist, and the
11531               	; 	'     torso's bottom row and the legs' top row do not align across it --
11532               	; 	'     green shows through and he reads as coming apart.

12019               	; 	' ======================================================================
12020               	; 	' THE SCANNER
12021               	; 	' ======================================================================
12022               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12023               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12024               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12025               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12026               	; 	'
12027               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12028               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12029               	; 	'
12030               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12031               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12032               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12033               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12034               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12035               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12036               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12037               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12038               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12039               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12040               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12041               	; esc_tick:
12042               cvb_ESC_TICK
12043               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
12044               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12045               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12046               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).

12066               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12067               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12068               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12069               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12070               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12071               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12072               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12073               	; 	'
12074               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12075               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12076               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12077               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12078               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12079               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12080               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12377               	;
12378               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12379               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12380               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12381               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12382               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12383               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12384               	; 	'
12385               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12386               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12387               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12388               	; 	'
12389               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12390               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12391               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12392               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12393               	; 	'
12394               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12395               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12396               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12397               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12398               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12399               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12400               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12401               	; 	'
12402               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12403               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12404               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12405               	; 	'
12406               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12407               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12408               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.

12751               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12752               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12753               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12754               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12755               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12756               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12757               	; scan_wipe:
12758               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
12759               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12760               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12761               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12762               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12763               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12764               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12765               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12766               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12767               	; 	'
12768               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12769               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12770               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12771               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12772               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12773               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12774               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12775               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12776               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12777               	; 	'
12778               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12779               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12780               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12781               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12782               	; 	'
12783               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
12784               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

12871               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.

13795               	;
13796               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13797               	; 	'
13798               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13799               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13800               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13801               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13802               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13803               	; 	'
13804               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13805               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13806               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13807               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13808               	; 	' counting stops.
13809               	;
13810               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13811               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13812               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13813               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13814               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13815               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
13816               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
13817               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
13818               	; 	'
13819               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
13820               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
13821               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

13976               	;
13977               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay
13978               	; 	' counters are not ticked inside this loop -- a tone still sounding when
13979               	; 	' the pause starts would hang for its whole duration, which is the classic
13980               	; 	' CVBasic sticky-audio failure.

13982               	; 	' ticked by the main loop, so anything still sounding when the loop stops
13983               	; 	' -- for a capture, a death, the bonus count -- sustains for as long as
13984               	; 	' whatever replaced the loop takes. That is where the long beep over the
13985               	; 	' bonus tally came from: not the tally's own note, which turns itself off
13986               	; 	' after every unit, but a footstep or a hit that was still ringing when

14423               	;
14424               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14425               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14426               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14427               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14428               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14429               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14430               	;
14431               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14432               	; 	'
14433               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14434               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14435               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14436               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14437               	; 	'
14438               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14439               	; 	'
14440               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14441               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14442               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14443               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14444               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14445               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14446               	; 	'
14447               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14448               	; 	'
14449               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14450               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14451               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14452               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14453               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14454               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14455               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14456               	; 	'
14457               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14458               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14459               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14460               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14461               	; 	'
14462               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14463               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14464               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14465               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14466               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14467               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14468               	; 	'
14469               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14470               	; 	'
14471               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14472               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14473               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14474               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14475               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14476               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
14477               	; 	' back to 7.

14601               	;
14602               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14603               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14604               	; 	'
14605               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14606               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14607               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14608               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14609               	; 	'
14610               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14611               	; 	'
14612               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14613               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14614               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14615               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14616               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14617               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14618               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14619               	; 	'
14620               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14621               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14622               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14623               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14624               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14625               	; 	'
14626               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14627               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14628               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14629               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14630               	; 	#if TI994A
14631               	; 	BANK 2
14632      01CC     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

15296               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15297               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15298               	; 	'
15299               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15300               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15301               	; 	' being small sprites.
15302               	; 	'
15303               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15304               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15305               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15306               	; 	'
15307               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15308               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15309               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15310               	;
15311               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15312               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16568               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16569               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16570               	; 	'
16571               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16572               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16573               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16574               	; 	'
16575               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16576               	; 	' blit is
16577               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16578               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16579               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16580               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16581               	; 	'
16582               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16583               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16584               	; 	'
16585               	; 	' template ids:
16586               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16587               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16588               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16589               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16590               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16591               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16592               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16593               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16594               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16595               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16596               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16597               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16598               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16599               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
